text: There was amusement "off" as well as on, during The Gondoliers' season. For instance the Gondola which nightly "sailed" on to the stage of the Theatre Royal has printed on it (not viewable by the audience) the words: "Italian Gondola made in Hongkong."

label: text
text: The hydro-aeroplane of Mr. Harry W. Abbott of Kowloon which drifted away from Paranaque, near Manila, on Tuesday of last week, has not been found, according to the Cavite naval station. A reward of P.50 has been offered by Mr. Abbott for information leading to the finding of the plane.

label: text
text: Messrs. Lammert Brothers, at their auction rooms in Duddell Street, yesterday, conducted a public auction of the leasehold property. No. 16 and 18, Queen's Road Central. Bidding began at $200,000 and the property which was in one lot, was eventually knocked down to Mr. P. K. Kwok for $271,500.

label: text
text: The return of notifiable diseases in the Colony for the week ended on March 28 showed 1 Swiss "case of diphtheria, 5 Chinese cases of small-pox, 2 of which were fatal, 6 Chinese cases of enteric fever from which 5 deaths resulted, 5 Chinese cases of cerebrospinal fever, of which 4 proved fatal and 1 Chinese case of puerperal fever. The return for the 24 hours ended on March 30 shows 2 cases of diphtheria, 1 of enteric fever, and 2 of cerebrospinal fever, all Chinese.

label: text
text: In 1910 Alberta, Canada, had 294,255 horses; it now has more than 875,000; its cattle have increased from 1,051,407 to 1,629,815; hogs, 143,560 to 949,891; sheep, 179,067 to 206,458.

label: text
text: Owing to lack of support it has been found necessary to cancel the performance of "The Gondoliers by the Philharmonic Society to-night. The proceeds were to have been given to the Hongkong Benevolent Society.

label: text
text: Medical inspection of children attending the schools operated by the Shanghai Municipal Council was proposed at a meeting of the Council Committee on Foreign Education. After considerable discussion, it was agreed that a report on the matter should be asked from the Commissioner of Public Health in order to learn whether some system of periodical inspection of school children could be devised with the staff now at his disposal, it being considered that much valuable assistance and advice could be rendered by the nurses in the Council's service.

label: text
text: "Little Hsu," General Hsu Shutseng, is returning to Peking vid Russia and is expected to be figuring on the Chinese political stage again within a couple of months. It is reported that Marshal Chang Tso-lin offers no objections to his re-employment, especially as he has been recommended for service by General Lu Yung-hsiang, Tupan of Kiangsu. It is believed that his first appointment will be Vice-Minister of War in charge of the Luchunpu as General Wu Kwang-hsin desires retirement.

label: text
text:
The number of registered bee-keepers in Manitoba increased from 1,200 to 1,800 between 1928 and 1924. The aggregate value of the honey production in 1924 was $200,000 net to the producers. Bee-keeping has developed to such an extent that the western demand is now chiefly met by home production, and factories for making apintry supplies have been established.
In Bengal the Automobile Association does not seem adequately supported. Out of 12,700 registered private owners, but 2,000 belong to the Association, though that is an increase on the former numbers.

text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL.

label: text
text: The wife of a farmer in the Taingkianpu district has given birth to a baby boy with the body of a snake, about six feet long, two noses, two mouths and four eyes, (says the Chinese press). The "infant" could speak as soon as he was born, we are further told, "but nobody could understand him." Attempts were made to strangle him, but when these failed he was hit across the head with a heavy stick and killed. The body was later hung up on a tree.

label: text
text: A house which is one of the claimants to the title of having been the home of Dickéus' little Noll this just had a narrow escape from being burned down. This is a shop in Portsmouth Street, Lincoln's Inn Fields, visited by numerous tourists as the Old Curiosity Shop of renown. It has just passed to new tenants, and workmen employed on the interior left a fire burning in one of the rooms. Smoke was seen by passers-by at night, and the fire brigade being summoned fortunately arrived in good time to prevent any considerable damage.

label: text
text: The effect of the present Canadian immigration policy in encouraging farmers, farm labourers, and female household workers to come to Canada is indicated by a recent analysis according to occupation of immigrants arriving in Canada since 1920. In 1920 32 per cent. of the total immigration were agriculturists and, domestics, and in 1921 35 per cent. Since then the ratio of agriculturists and domestics toward all immigration has been steadily increasing, being 44 per cent. for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1923, 47 per cent. for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1924; and 51 per cent. for the nine months April to December inclusive of 1924. In these nine months the total immigration to Canada was 100,570, of which agriculturists and domestics represented 51,056.

label: text
text: The appointment of Mr. James Blair to the position of manager of the London branch office of the Nippon Yusen Kalsha has been very cordially received in London shipping circles, in which his high ability and tactful courtesy are felt in the highest esteem. This is the first occasion that a European talk held this appointment since the death of Captain James, RN in 1910, in which year Mr. Blair was made a sub-manager. Mr. Blair for his services during the Russo-Japan war was decorated with the 5th Order of the Rising Sun, while in acknowledgment of his excellent work during the Great War he received the 4th Order of the same honour.

label: text
text: Hongkong theatregoers should be interested in the following:—It is only putting it mildly when one describes the staging of Reginald Berkeley's light comedy "French Leave," by the Hankow A.D.C. at the Victoria Hall as an unqualified success, says the C.C. Post." A bumper house attended and rocked with laughter right throughout the three acts, for the characters were interpreted by the caste with that verve which is so absolutely necessary to make a farce irresistibly humorous and yet not grotesque. Mrs. F.C.R. Keed was the heroine, "Mile Jullette," Mme. Labinsky played "Mme. Peaux," Mr. C.S. Cheetham was "Capt. Harry Glenister" and Mr Walter Neill "Brig. General Archilbald Root."

text: We hear very little of Queen Alexandra nowadays, says a Home writer. Her life at Sandringham is very secluded, but she nearly always has friends or relations staying with her. text: The cross-word idea is getting to such absurd lengths that the Cosmo Club in London is arranging a teadance, at which members will be given paper caps on which are parts of words. A man with the letters "B" or his cap will have to find a partner from among those women with say "Fore or" An on their caps. Slips with complete words written on them will be put into a hat and when one is drawn the couple who have made that word between their two caps will receive some present or other.

The Queen wore large goggles to protect her eyes when she entered the artificial sunlight room in paying a surprise visit with Ledy Desborough to St Thomas's Hospital. After watching the children enjoying themselves in the brilliant rays of the mercury vapour lamps, the Queen visited the Mary Ward for maternity cases. She was greatly interested in an adjoining room filled with cois in which were babies, some only a few days old.
The announcement that the Prices of Wales is to visit Uruguay and Chile as well as the Avenue has slipped out in a curiously casual way. It is the first time that an heir to the British Throne has visited South America, and it is a great commitment to the Prince and to the British nation that he should receive these cordial invitations from three of the leading Spanish-American publics. Moreover, it is not only filtering, but there is good business in it also.
